Nineteen comments

Paddy Reynold’s Jig

Paddy Reynold’s is a current NYC fiddler who was raised in Killavill, Co. Sligo - the breeding ground of some of the best Fiddlers. This tune may seem tricky because of the key but it is a wonderful fiddle tune & not really all that hard to play. I got this setting from Tony Demarco & Brian Conway’s album “Apple in Winter”.

↳ Posted by b.maloney on November 5th, 2001.

Oops!!

This is called Dave Collins’s jig not Paddy Reynold’s. I think Dave is a relation to Kathleen Collins, I think they are Brother & Sister. The whole Collins family was involved one way or another with music & dance.

↳ Posted by b.maloney on November 5th, 2001.

Tecnical note

Sorry to get technical, but it’s in B flat rather than F. It happens that E flat, the 4th degree of the scale, is not used anywhere in this tune (it is hexatonic), so you can get away with just the B flat in the key signature… Or perhaps if the 4th WERE used it would be E natural, making it B flat Lydian.

↳ Posted by CreadurMawnOrganig on November 9th, 2001.

Your right - it’s in Bb Major but that wasn’t an option on the input screen.
I coiuld’ve posted it in GDor. (Two Flats) but would be very misleading to someone going by modal reference. So I left it in F.

At least someone noticed the tune!

Dave Collins’, X:5

Here is a setting in D as played by Charlie and Tommy Mulvihill here:
https://www.itma.ie/newyork/collections/charlie-mulvihill-collection
I think that Charlie played either a one-row box in D, or a two-row box with a D row
(either C#/D or D/C#). So it makes sense that he would prefer this setting in D.
